en.fit: No complementarity, and the easiest entrant to miss — the registry lists the condition as spinocerebellar palsy rather than ataxia, so a routine keyword scan passes straight over it.

forms: Collaboration not applicable
Monitoring priorities: start June 2026, primary completion June 2028, site in Warsaw
If its intranasal route proves feasible it undercuts the rationale for intravenous delivery
en.priorityWhy: Finding it at all exposes a blind spot in the daily scan: screening only on 'spinocerebellar ataxia' misses trials registered under other disease names. The scan criteria should be widened to include variants such as spinocerebellar palsy.

en.fit: No mechanistic room for complementarity: VO659 is an allele-preferential ASO aimed at the expanded CAG repeat itself, applicable across HD, SCA1 and SCA3. It addresses the cause where Steminent addresses the consequence.
en.whyNotRival: The only one of the three principal rivals still alive, and it competes for the same SCA1 and SCA3 patients. Yet it has no SCA efficacy data at all, extrapolating entirely from HD, and faces the same deep cerebellar and brainstem delivery ceiling that killed BIIB132. The competitive story reduces to this: VO659 hits the cause but cannot reach the tissue; Stemchymal reaches the tissue but addresses the consequence.
forms: Collaboration not applicable
Monitoring priority: the first SCA1/SCA3 biomarker readout, expected 2026–27, is the key catalyst
Its radiculitis safety signal warrants continued tracking
en.priorityWhy: The threat is prospective but the catalyst is well defined. A positive readout would let the upstream-silencing narrative override broad neuroprotection; a failure or worsening safety signal would strengthen the delivery argument for cell therapy. Both outcomes need a prepared response.

fit: 無互補面。Troriluzole 兩個隨機對照試驗都沒過主要終點，改用回溯式外部對照 RWE 送 NDA，FDA 於 2025-11-04 發出完全回應信駁回。

Its value to Steminent is almost entirely cautionary: do not rest an approval on RWE or external controls, since the FDA has rejected a run of externally controlled rare disease filings; a nominal SCA3 subgroup signal will not carry a licence; and where the disease is slow and the effect weak, a more sensitive scale does not rescue the result.
forms: Collaboration not applicable
A counter-example for external control strategy — which bears directly on the DZNE/ESMI route: if Steminent uses an external control it must be done more rigorously than this
en.priorityWhy: Low priority with intelligence already sufficient, given the seventeen-page competitor teardown already on file. Continued tracking is enough.

Monitoring priority: its readout will be the first substantive answer on the polyQ siRNA route
Any future move into SCA2 needs a differentiated rationale and must avoid Taiwanese sites
en.priorityWhy: Low priority. SCA2 is not among Steminent's focus indications — its own map advises holding back — and the Taiwanese site is already occupied.

en.fit: Its link to MSA is mechanistic adjacency rather than direct competition: MSA and Parkinson's are both synucleinopathies, but MSA pathology sits in oligodendrocytes and Parkinson's in neurons, so a drug does not necessarily carry across.

Monitoring priority: clinical validation of the TV platform rather than DNL422 itself
en.priorityWhy: Low priority, but the monitoring angle matters: the question is not whether it enters MSA but whether someone else solves the structural bottleneck of blood-brain-barrier delivery.
